title: The same bug is invisible when the audit field is absent
prompt: What does this return? Read it — do not run it.

given.script:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
ns soap http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/
ns cust http://acme.com/customer
---
payload.soap#Envelope.soap#Body.cust#GetCustomersResponse.*cust#Customer map {
  id: $.@id,
  name: $.cust#Name,
  status: $.Status
}

solution:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
ns soap http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/
ns cust http://acme.com/customer
---
payload.soap#Envelope.soap#Body.cust#GetCustomersResponse.*cust#Customer map {
  id: $.@id,
  name: $.cust#Name,
  status: $.Status
}

explanation.approach: With no `audit:Status` sibling, `cust:Status` is the only element with that local name, so the bare selector reaches it and the wrong script happens to produce the right answer. A test suite built only from records like this one would never catch the bug.
